name: reactions
title: Reactions
description: What a room says about one message without typing. Pills sit under the message and count up, the one the reader pressed is filled and outlined where the rest are flat, and the row adds its height to the message once and never again, because the set of emotes is fixed. The picker floats over the stream and reflows nothing, which is why it is positioned rather than mounted in the column: a picker arriving in flow would push every message under it at the moment the reader is aiming at one. The emotes are the host's, the same four specimen 4h floats, and the library ships none and names none. There is no free text here, so nothing in this control needs screening, and nothing in it is ranked, stored or counted by the library.
docs: Pass the whole fixed set as `emotes`, in the order you want them read, and the same set every time: the row's claim is that it adds its height once, and a set that grows breaks it. Only emotes with a count, or the reader's own, draw a pill; the rest live in the picker, and a message nobody has reacted to renders nothing at all. An emote with no word to draw, such as a heart, passes a `mark` node and keeps its `label` for anybody reading it out. The counts are yours: `onReact` fires for adding and for taking back, and the component changes no number by itself. `picking` opens the picker and is yours too, because the long press that opens it lands on the message and the message is a different component; the picker does not close itself on a pick, so `onPick` both records the emote and clears `picking`.
